Gut‒liver‒brain axis signature of cirrhosis-related cognitive impairment is consistent across multi-national cohorts.

This study examined whether gut microbiome signatures associated with cognitive impairment in cirrhosis are consistent across patients from the USA, Denmark, Lithuania, and Mexico. Using stool shotgun metagenomic sequencing and psychometric testing for covert hepatic encephalopathy, the authors identified taxonomic and functional microbial associations with cognitive scores that held across all four national cohorts. The findings suggest a reproducible gut‒liver‒brain axis signature despite geographic differences in diet and clinical practice.

iScience 2026-11-20 Medium

Multi-scale hybrid correction of noisy long reads.

DADEC is a new hybrid error-correction method for noisy long reads that uses a three-stage confidence-ordered framework: stringent de Bruijn graph correction, haplotype-aware short-read alignment refinement, and permissive de Bruijn graph recovery. Across seven simulated and three real datasets, it achieved the lowest mismatch and indel rates in most benchmarks while preserving genuine biological variation and avoiding over-correction.

A specialized microbiome enriched in nitrification and halogen cycling potential resolved from multi-omics investigation of a Caribbean suboxic and acidic marine sinkhole.

This study characterizes the microbiome of an unusual acidic, suboxic submerged 'lake' within the Luymes Sinkholes in the Caribbean, using 59 size-fractionated samples analyzed with multi-omics approaches. The authors resolve a specialized microbial community enriched in nitrification and halogen cycling potential, showing how microbes adapt to extreme deviations from normal oceanographic conditions including low pH, low oxygen, and elevated inorganic nutrients.

Aerobic methane oxidation by microorganisms exacerbates neurotoxic methylmercury accumulation in rice paddy fields.

A large-scale field survey across China's rice-growing regions, combined with 13CH4-DNA stable isotope probing, reveals a positive association between aerobic methane oxidation and microbial mercury methylation in paddy soils. This suggests that methanotrophs contribute to the production of neurotoxic methylmercury that accumulates in rice, linking methane cycling to mercury risk in a major food system.

PEONY: a global reference database of DNA viral (vOTU) sequences from viral size-fractionated metagenomes (viromes).

PEONY is an updated global reference database of DNA viral sequences (vOTUs, mostly dsDNA bacteriophages) derived exclusively from virus size-fractionated metagenomes (viromes) across global ecosystems. The update rebrands the former Phages and Integrated Genomes Encapsidated or Not database to reflect its stricter inclusion of only encapsidated, virome-derived viral sequences.

This paper presents an optimized super-SILAC (stable isotope labeling by amino acids in cell culture) strategy specifically designed to quantify low-abundance non-acetyl histone acyl modifications in gut epithelial tissue. By generating a heavy-labeled internal standard from colon cells, the method improves reliable profiling of histone post-translational modifications linked to microbiota-derived metabolites and acute inflammation.
